task: Figure out which parent-teacher conference slots to book first, before registration opens, based on how the kids are doing in school.
transcript: Opened the app: a Home screen asking 'What can I help with?' with three example prompts and a note that nothing is sent without my OK.
Typed my question about which conference slots to book first for Rafi, Ezra and Noa and tapped Send; it showed 'Getting started' with dots.
Waited 30s: the chat got a title 'Pick parent-teacher conference slots', said 'Your family school helper is on it' and 'Working on it'.

Waited 30s more: answer arrived. The sign-up is Lincoln Middle only, so it covers Ezra (up to 4 slots): 1) Mr. Brandt, Math, C+ with 3 missing assignments, 2) Mr. Ruiz, Science, B with a lab report due Mon Nov 16 not in, 3) English (A-) and Social Studies (A) optional.

Scrolled down: for Rafi it said Maple has not announced conferences, his reading is 'approaching grade level', 2 reading logs missing, and offered a draft email to Ms. Ortiz marked 'Draft email, not sent' with Open in Mail and Copy buttons.
Scrolled down: for Noa it said nothing about her school or grades was in my email, then offered a reminder at 6:55pm Sunday before sign-ups open.
Typed a follow-up asking which times for Ezra would not clash with my calendar and tapped Send.
Waited about 3 minutes with 'Working on it'; after 2 minutes it added 'Reading email and calendar can take a few minutes', which reassured me.

Answer arrived: the school email has no conference dates, sign-ups open Sun Nov 15 at 7pm; avoid Mon Nov 16 3:00-4:45 (Ezra's dentist) and Wed Nov 18 after about 5:15 (Noa's piano recital); book Brandt and Ruiz back to back; paste the open times once sign-ups open and it will pick the best two.
Scrolled up to read the start of that answer, then finished.
stumbles: The first answer ranked teachers but gave no actual times; I had to ask a follow-up to get the calendar clashes.
The follow-up took about 3 minutes with only 'Working on it' dots, longer than ChatGPT.
Small inconsistency: it said I can book up to 4 slots, then offered to 'pick the best two'.
The calendar answer had to be scrolled up to read its first line, since the screen opened at the end of the reply.
verdict: It told me clearly to book Ezra's math and science teachers first, explained why from his grades, handled Rafi with a ready, unsent email draft, and was honest that it knew nothing about Noa. A follow-up gave the real calendar clashes to avoid, though it was slower than ChatGPT and I had to ask twice to get times.
